children:
The Link Between Falling Energy Prices and Inflation Expectations

In April, US inflation surged to its fastest pace in three years, driven by energy prices. High energy costs solidified market expectations that the Federal Reserve would maintain high interest rates until next year, with some even suggesting a possible rate hike before the end of the year. Gold, as a non-interest-bearing asset, is naturally under pressure in a high-interest-rate environment due to increased holding costs and the enhanced attractiveness of the US dollar.

However, falling oil prices are providing potential support for gold through the inflation transmission mechanism. Analysts point out that "gold and oil prices maintain a negative correlation; oil prices influence inflation and monetary policy. Lower oil prices reduce the probability of interest rate hikes, which is beneficial for gold." If the resumption of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz is implemented, it will directly alleviate energy-driven inflationary pressures, weakening the need for the Federal Reserve to further tighten policy, thus providing gold with medium-term breathing room.

However, the current market is still dominated by interest rate paths. In May, global markets were in a consolidation phase. Geopolitical tensions and inflation concerns continued to affect sentiment, but easing safe-haven demand and the high-interest-rate outlook jointly suppressed the performance of precious metals. Traders are closely watching the Federal Reserve's subsequent statements and whether energy prices can continue to fall in order to avoid a resurgence of inflation expectations.
